name: Jār Allāh Abū al-Qāsim Maḥmūd ibn ʿUmar al-Zamakhsharī
summary: The Khwārazmian master of the Arabic sciences, author of the Qurʾān commentary al-Kashshāf and of al-Mufaṣṣal, the compact grammar on which Ibn Yaʿīsh wrote his great commentary.
bio: Al-Zamakhsharī was born in Zamakhshar in Khwārazm in 467/1075, a Persian who made Arabic his life's work and who held, in the preface of al-Mufaṣṣal, that Arabic was the language every science needs. He studied in Bukhara and Baghdad and lived for years in Mecca, which earned him the name Jār Allāh, 'God's neighbour'. He was a Ḥanafī in law and a Muʿtazilī in theology, and said so openly. He walked on a wooden leg; the biographers give two explanations, frost on a winter journey, which he gave himself, and a story from his childhood, when he broke the leg of a bird he had tied with a string and his mother wished the same on him.

His al-Mufaṣṣal (finished 515/1121) arranges grammar in four parts, the noun, the verb, the particle and what they share (the phonology and morphology of the words), in short sections; it became a school text from Khwārazm to Syria, and Ibn Yaʿīsh's Sharḥ al-Mufaṣṣal and Ibn al-Ḥājib's al-Īḍāḥ are commentaries on it. His shorter al-Unmūdhaj gave a first course. His al-Kashshāf reads the Qurʾān through its grammar and rhetoric and was commented on for centuries, by Sunni scholars who corrected its theology as they went. He also made the dictionary Asās al-balāgha. He died in Jurjāniyya in Khwārazm in 538/1144.
